audit.why: 55.20% over 692 games — a strongly favoured lane on a large sample.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives K'Sante four stages and Ambessa zero on a lane she wins 55.20% of the time, and it contradicts the prose three times: whys[2] says level 3 'out-trades him', whys[4] says level 6 flips it, and whys[5] plus late call first item 'your peak' where 'you win the straight duel'.
audit.why: This is a clean early-favoured lane with a hard scaling opponent. Ambessa owns 3, 6 and first item; K'Sante owns the 4-5 cooldown gap and everything past two tank items.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Skill / Ambessa / K'Sante / Ambessa / Ambessa / K'Sante in both layers — Ambessa 3, K'Sante 2, Skill 2, which fits 55.20% and matches every why on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out is discussed three times without its cooldown, and Ambessa's own level 6 and first-item spikes are credited to 'R's flat armor pen' — which is in Riot's text for none of her abilities.
audit.why: All Out is 120/100/80 seconds and it is the rare ultimate that makes its user WORSE defensively: Riot's text is 'increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defenses'. It also removes the knockback and stun from Path Maker while active, so an All Out K'Sante has traded away his own peel. Against Ambessa that means his ultimate is a window she wants opened, not one she has to survive — which is a much better reason to fight at 6 than a penetration stat that does not exist.
audit.corrected: 120s and the reduced-defences trade stated in whys[4], whys[6], spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text and phases[4].why. Penetration claims removed from whys[4], spikes[2].text, mid and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names none of K'Sante's five abilities, and the one piece of hard CC it does describe is wrong. It refers to 'his Q3 knockup' three times. Riot's Ntofo Strikes: 'On hit, grants a stack of Ntofo Strikes. At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in.' Two stacks, not three, and it is a PULL, not a knockup. Footwork (E) — a 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s dash that grants a shield — is missing from the page entirely.
audit.why: Pull versus knockup reverses the positioning consequence: a knockup interrupts you where you stand, a pull drags you into his melee range and into Dauntless Instinct's marked follow-up attack. Two stacks rather than three also means it arrives a full ability sooner than the page implies, on a 3.5-second base cooldown. And Footwork is the ability that actually beats an Ambessa combo — a shield on a 10-second dash is the burst window she needs forced out before committing, and the page never tells her it exists.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named. The two-stack shockwave pull corrected in mid, whys[3], wants.foe[1], dontsFull[0] and report[5].t. Footwork added to early, whys[1], whys[2], spikes[0].text, wants.you[1], phases[2].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere on the page, so 'punish the moment his W charge is spent' has nothing to count against.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is a flat 3.5 seconds, Footwork is 10 down to 8, and Path Maker is 14 down to 10. Path Maker is the long one and therefore the correct thing to bait — but Footwork refilling every 10 seconds is why a single baited W is not enough on its own, and that is the sequencing the page was missing.
audit.corrected: All three numbers stated, with the all-in keyed to Path Maker AND Footwork both being down rather than W alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, though the full layer's late-game line already says 'anti-heal stays core'.
audit.why: All Out grants healing for its duration. Since it is also the moment his defences drop, it is precisely the window Ambessa wants to fight in — and the only thing that can rob her of that trade is his healing outpacing her burst.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal named in late, spikes[3].text and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out's opening knockback through terrain is never mentioned, though the page does correctly say he uses R to 'isolate you'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'K'Sante knocks an enemy back, launching them through any wall in their path.' That is HOW the isolation happens — you end up on the far side of a wall, away from your team, with a dash-empowered K'Sante following. Knowing it comes with terrain displacement changes where you are willing to stand near him.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is even — you have one ability up, long cooldowns, and his percent-HP passive plus charged-W mitigation mean you can't just walk in. Last-hit at the tip of your Q cone and don't throw Lacerate to chase. His W is a charged dash, not a Yasuo wall: while charging he gains damage reduction and on release he dashes and knocks up — so if you commit your empowered auto or Q2 slam into his charge, the reduction eats most of it and he dashes out, bait it first. At Level 3 your full short combo comes online and you start winning the dash-weave trade, since he has no sustained poke and can't escape once Lacerate's slow is on him.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is even — you have one ability up, long cooldowns, and Dauntless Instinct marks you for bonus damage on his next attack. Last-hit at the tip of your Q cone and don't throw Lacerate to chase. Path Maker (W) is a charged dash: while charging he takes reduced damage, then he dashes out knocking back and stunning — so committing your empowered auto or Sundering Slam into the charge just feeds the reduction. Bait it, and force out Footwork (E) too: a 10-second dash that shields him is what really eats your burst. At Level 3 your full short combo comes online and the dash-weave starts winning.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his cleanest window — your cooldowns are at their longest and his Q3 knockup plus W dash let him trade and walk away, so farm and don't force here. Level 6 flips it: Public Execution blinks you behind him, then suppresses and stuns — it ignores the W dash he'd peel with, and your R's flat armor pen still bites because his resists are tank-high but unitemized. Punish the moment his W charge is spent. Dodge his Q line — its third hit is his only hard CC and the one thing that interrupts your dash chain — and never all-in while it's up.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his cleanest window — your cooldowns are longest while Ntofo Strikes (Q) returns every 3.5 seconds, so farm and don't force here. Level 6 flips it: Public Execution blinks 1250 units, suppresses and stuns, and All Out answers only by costing him his own defences. Punish once Path Maker's charge is spent and Footwork's shield is down. Learn his real CC too: two Ntofo Strikes stacks fire a shockwave that PULLS you in, so it drags you into his marked follow-up rather than knocking you off it.

edits.before: Your first-item Eclipse spike with Q maxed is your peak — Q1-auto-Q2 halves him while you stay full, and you win the straight duel here. But K'Sante is a hard scaler: once he finishes two tank items his percent-HP plus W damage reduction soak your combo, and his R sheds his own armor and MR to turn duelist and isolate you for the all-in — your damage is physical-only, so stacked armor and his AD-form scaling catch up. Win this lane before two items land. Past that, group and let his team-side scaling be someone else's problem.
edits.after: Your first-item Eclipse spike with Q maxed is your peak — Q1-auto-Q2 halves him while you stay full, and you win the straight duel here. But K'Sante is a hard scaler: two tank items plus Path Maker's charge reduction soak your combo, and All Out sheds his own resists to turn duelist while healing him, so keep Grievous Wounds on him. Its opening knockback launches you through any wall in the way — that is how the isolation happens. Win before two items land, then let his scaling be someone else's problem.

notes: The 'never names any of K'Sante's abilities' defect was real and it hid a wrong mechanic: the page said 'Q3 knockup' three times, when Ntofo Strikes fires its shockwave at TWO stacks and it PULLS rather than knocks up. Pull versus knockup is the difference between being interrupted where you stand and being dragged into his marked follow-up attack. Footwork was also completely absent — a 10-second dash-plus-shield is the ability that actually beats an Ambessa burst, and the derived data flagged exactly that. Two derived flags I did NOT use: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json puts 'trueDamage' on Path Maker and the interactions file says 'K'Sante bypasses stacking resistances (Path Maker (W)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here'. Riot's description of Path Maker says nothing about true damage, so per the brief I trusted the description and left the claim out; if the flag is right it is a significant itemization point and deserves confirming. Unverified and removed rather than restated: Ambessa's 'R's flat armor pen' (four fields here), and the 'percent-HP passive' attributed to Dauntless Instinct, which Riot describes purely as a damage-amplifying mark plus an All Out damage bonus.
